questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Safety, a good wide offer of law courses in english

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Switzerland is more expensive than I realised, so being able to buy basic necessities were often a struggle. Lots of unforeseen bills, incredibly difficult to communicate with any official institutions and companies in Switzerland. I recommend living in the student housing, as I didn't secure a place in time, and it was hard to connect with the other exchange students living in a different place. I would have chosen a different destination to go on an exchange to if I could re-do it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the welcome week and offering of information was very well-coordinated, and the office supplying information to incoming exchange students answered your questions/e-mails swiftly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The official program, and then I sent a few e-mails asking for answers to practical issues, and I always received assistance quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The incoming mobility coordinator recommended some websites to search through, and I found a place there. I recommend finding a place to stay very much in advance, a few months before if possible. There were not many options, and I found an okay place to live - however, it was costly and natives Swiss told me I was being ripped off.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It might be challenging to connect with the other exchange students if you choose to live off-campus; however, it was nice to have your place to stay instead of sharing a flat with multiple people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far I recall, the mobility coordinators were very helpful and did most of the work for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lots of help from the university mobility coordinators

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered and got all the classes I wanted. It is very easy to register.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask any questions you might have no matter how small or "stupid" they seem, you might be surprised how practicial/administrative stuff works in Swiss universities. The coordinators are patient and kind.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses amounted to 5 ECTS each, however, I felt the burden of work was the same as 15 ECTS courses in Denmark, which made the exam season/preparation incredibly stressful but manageable with coordination and discipline.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar - some classes required class participation, but it only impacted a smaller percentage of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Current Issues in Human Rights Law, Internet Law, Introduction to the Common Law System, Introduction to Swiss Law, Law of Sustainable Development, and International Humanitarian Law.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Humanitarian Law was very interesting, as well as Internet Law. The professors also made it easy to participate, as they posted video podcasts of each class. I appreciate the flexible style of teaching.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Registration for arriving at the canton/leaving the canton, the exorbitant transport prices, a bill of around 350 francs for a license (TV/Internet tax) despite not owning a TV or knowing any Swiss media outlets

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport prices were unreasonably high when my mother visited me. She spent 1000 DKK in one day for transport only (for about 1.30 hours of transport) necessities, trash bags were over 100 DKK for ten bags.. etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was pleasantly surprised by the sports opportunities at the university! free good quality sports classes multiple times a week, and even a free gym you could go independently and use all the exercise machines needed.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sports classes, which I used a lot. I can really recommend taking advantage of the sports classes. There were some social events organised, but it was rare and often chaotic, however I appreciate the availability.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Its really expensive to travel around Switzerland however if you can afford it, I recommend visiting other areas of Switzerland. Theres also many great parks and forests in Luzern.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is similar to the danish culture, however I arrived during FassNact which was a huge culture shock and definitely put a damper to my enthusiasm.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living in the student housing and participating in the Erasmus social activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swiss often not wanting to speak English

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hiking culture, appreciation of nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have a good savings account or otherwise healthy economy, alternatively, apply for grants, you will appreciate it when you arrive! Also make sure to live in the student housing, if you want a social experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The most important thing is really considering your economy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting and making friends with Swiss people, however I did that independent from the University.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Personal finances and socializing with other exchange students

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
